mina: RFC follow-up: propose a lightweight 'onboard-pacer' that shards probe budget and guarantees a tiny ramp floor so low-priority models make progress during bursts. Goal: reduce KV thrash and keep golden coverage high.

jorge: +1. Key signals: recent_ingest_qps, expected_token_cost (from registry profile), and seqlen_hint. Cost score = ingest_qps * token_cost * seqlen_weight.

sam: implementation notes: intake assigns shard = hash(model_id)%N_shards. Each shard gets budget_slice = global_budget * shard_share. Per-model allowance = shard_slice * priority_weight, then apply min_probe_rps floor and linear ramp over ramp_window_s.

lia: correctness checks (tokenizer parity, logits sanity) must run before any perf probes and be exempt from pacing. Also, record the effective_probe_plan with the model artifact for reproducibility.

mina: prober behavior: two LRU buckets (golden, other). When kv_util > kv_safe_threshold, evict from other-first. Cap unique_prefixes_per_prober and apply TTL decay for stale prefixes.

sam: success criteria for sim: golden_coverage >=0.8 within 30m for 90% of models; kv_miss_rate <5%; low-priority median time-to-deepbench <50m in rush case. I'll run steady + rush (200 models / 10m) traces.

jorge: dedicated pools must be honored: if deployment_hint==dedicated_reserved and reserved_capacity >= required_capacity, skip global shard throttle.

ops-bot: staging: onboard-pacer v0.1 attached to prebench staging queue.

mina: action items: mina draft RFC with config schema; sam produce sims and dashboards; jorge add registry seqlen hints; lia write acceptance checks. Target RFC by week end. If you have edge cases (tiny declared token_costs, tenant hotspots) add here.
